samples.summary: New behavior — a table block inside a cross-block selection is read whole (visitTable, incl. nested-table recursion and colSpan===0 skip) — has no test
samples.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` adds a branch the old `getRangeStyleSummary` never had: for a top-level cross-block selection, a `block.type === 'table'` is walked entirely via `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:164-167), which also recurses into nested tables (line 75) and skips merged-away cells (line 73). The old code in editor.ts simply read the table block's (empty) `inlines`, so this is a real behavior change. The new suite `packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts` only builds (a) a single-paragraph doc, (b) a Heading 6 doc, (c) a header table where the selection stays inside one cell — never a selection that spans a body paragraph and a table, never a nested table, never a merged cell. Grepping `packages/docs/test` for `tableCellRange`/`getRangeStyleSummary` turns up only editor-range-style-summary.test.ts (flat paragraphs/headings), editor-step-selection-font-size.test.ts (stepSelectionFontSize, not the summary) and table-merge-context/cell-range-expand (unrelated).

samples.summary: New cell→parent-table endpoint normalization (selection spanning two different cells, or a cell and a body block) is untested
samples.evidence: range-runs.ts:146-150 introduces `anchorTopId = anchorCI ? anchorCI.tableBlockId : ...` so a selection whose endpoints live in *different* cells (or one in a cell, one at top level) now resolves to the enclosing table block and produces a summary; previously `getBlockIndex` failed and the old code returned an empty summary. No test in packages/docs/test exercises a cross-cell or cell↔body selection against `getRangeStyleSummary()` or the Cmd+B path — the new header-table test only selects two blocks inside the *same* cell (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts, 'header table cell range summary' describe).

samples.summary: Keyboard toggle now decides from the range for a table cell-rectangle selection, and that path has no test
samples.evidence: `resolveToggle` now calls `isStyleOnInSelection` (text-editor.ts:2895), which walks `visitStyledRunsInRange`; for `range.tableCellRange` that visits every block of every selected cell (range-runs.ts:86-101). Cmd/Ctrl+B over a rectangle of cells therefore changes verdict versus the previous caret-based decision. The new test file never sets a `tableCellRange` (no `tableCellRange` occurrence in backward-selection-toggle.test.ts); the only cell-rectangle tests in the package are for stepSelectionFontSize (editor-step-selection-font-size.test.ts:256) and merge context.

samples.summary: The `undefined` fallback branch of isStyleOnInSelection (selection holding no text runs) is not tested
samples.evidence: `isStyleOnInSelection` returns `undefined` when `sawRun` stays false — e.g. a selection spanning empty blocks or one whose runs are all zero-width — and `resolveToggle` then falls back to `!!visual[key]`. This documented fallback has no test: backward-selection-toggle.test.ts always selects non-empty runs, and no other docs test dispatches a bold shortcut over an empty-run selection.

samples.summary: The shared TextEditor toggle change also affects text boxes (docs + slides), but no test covers a keyboard toggle with a backward selection inside a text box
samples.evidence: `text-box-editor.ts:666` constructs the same `TextEditor` whose `resolveToggle` now consults `visitStyledRunsInRange(this.doc, ...)`. Text boxes have their own flat `getRangeStyleSummary` (text-box-editor.ts:1017) that was *not* routed through the new shared walk, so keyboard and toolbar could still diverge there — and nothing tests it. The new slides mobile-toolbar test stubs `SlidesTextBoxEditor` entirely (makeTextEditor), so it cannot exercise the real text-box engine.
searchedFor: Grep getRangeStyleSummary in packages/slides/src and packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts

samples.summary: Weak assertion: `expect(...).not.toBe(true)` passes for undefined/false/'mixed' — it would also pass if the summary silently returned nothing
samples.evidence: In 'caret style reports the preceding run while the summary reports the range' the range-side assertion is `expect(editor.getRangeStyleSummary().bold).not.toBe(true)`; an empty summary (the exact failure mode the header-cell part of this PR fixes) satisfies it. Asserting the concrete expected value (`undefined`, since the tail run carries no bold) would make the test able to fail for the right reason. Same pattern at the 'summary still reads true' test for `getSelectionStyle().bold`.

samples.summary: Frontend toggle tests assert only against a fully stubbed editor; nothing verifies the real editors produce the caret/range disagreement the stubs encode
samples.evidence: `makeEditor` returns hand-written `getSelectionStyle`/`getRangeStyleSummary` mocks, so these tests prove only that the component reads the summary — they cannot fail if the engine's summary is wrong for the selections they describe. For docs there is an engine-level counterpart (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts); for the slides text-box editor used by mobile-toolbar there is no equivalent engine test, so that toolbar's claim rests entirely on the mock. Minor because the component wiring is genuinely covered.

finding.summary: New behavior — a table block inside a cross-block selection is read whole (visitTable, incl. nested-table recursion and colSpan===0 skip) — has no test
finding.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` adds a branch the old `getRangeStyleSummary` never had: for a top-level cross-block selection, a `block.type === 'table'` is walked entirely via `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:164-167), which also recurses into nested tables (line 75) and skips merged-away cells (line 73). The old code in editor.ts simply read the table block's (empty) `inlines`, so this is a real behavior change. The new suite `packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts` only builds (a) a single-paragraph doc, (b) a Heading 6 doc, (c) a header table where the selection stays inside one cell — never a selection that spans a body paragraph and a table, never a nested table, never a merged cell. Grepping `packages/docs/test` for `tableCellRange`/`getRangeStyleSummary` turns up only editor-range-style-summary.test.ts (flat paragraphs/headings), editor-step-selection-font-size.test.ts (stepSelectionFontSize, not the summary) and table-merge-context/cell-range-expand (unrelated).

verdict.reason: The branch exists exactly as described (range-runs.ts:164-167 walks a whole table via visitTable; line 73 skips colSpan===0; lines 75-76 recurse into nested tables) and nothing reaches it in any test. visitStyledRunsInRange has only two call sites (editor.ts:2849 getRangeStyleSummary, text-editor.ts:3013 isRangeStyleAllOn); stepSelectionFontSizeImpl (editor.ts:1089-1126) duplicates its own walk and does not use the module. I enumerated every test that calls either entry point: editor-range-style-summary.test.ts contains no table at all (grep for tableData/insertTable/type:'table' → no matches); backward-selection-toggle.test.ts, read in full, uses a single paragraph (l.76-86), a Heading 6 block (l.225-232), and a header table whose selection has both endpoints inside one cell (l.355-397), which takes the same-cell branch at range-runs.ts:118-142, not line 164; editor-read-only.test.ts:254-274 uses one paragraph; pending-style-editor.test.ts has no table; text-box-editor.test.ts and step-font-size tests exercise different implementations. All frontend tests touching getRangeStyleSummary mock it (text-format-toggles.test.ts:41, docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx:44, toolbar-focus.test.ts:43). The closest candidate, table.test.ts:283 ('apply italic across paragraphs spanning a table'), only drives Doc.applyInlineStyle (the write path) and never the read walk, so it cannot fail if visitTable regresses. No range-runs unit test and no e2e specs exist. Per the rubric this is a behavior with no meaningful test (major).

finding.summary: Keyboard toggle now decides from the range for a table cell-rectangle selection, and that path has no test
finding.evidence: `resolveToggle` now calls `isStyleOnInSelection` (text-editor.ts:2895), which walks `visitStyledRunsInRange`; for `range.tableCellRange` that visits every block of every selected cell (range-runs.ts:86-101). Cmd/Ctrl+B over a rectangle of cells therefore changes verdict versus the previous caret-based decision. The new test file never sets a `tableCellRange` (no `tableCellRange` occurrence in backward-selection-toggle.test.ts); the only cell-rectangle tests in the package are for stepSelectionFontSize (editor-step-selection-font-size.test.ts:256) and merge context.

verdict.reason: The code path is real: toggleStyle resolves boolean keys through isStyleOnInSelection (text-editor.ts:2895) before dispatching to the tableCellRange branch (2914-2919), and isStyleOnInSelection (3007-3019) delegates to visitStyledRunsInRange, whose tableCellRange branch (range-runs.ts:86-101) walks every block of every selected cell — so a Cmd/Ctrl+B over a cell rectangle now derives add-vs-remove from all cells rather than the caret. No test covers that: the only tests touching tableCellRange are cell-range-expand.test.ts:145 (normalization), editor-step-selection-font-size.test.ts:253-272 (font-size stepping, not the boolean keyboard toggle), table-merge-context.test.ts:50/69/97 (merge context), and a frontend assertion of `tableCellRange: undefined`. The only keyboard-toggle test file, backward-selection-toggle.test.ts, covers single-block forward/backward ranges, Heading-6 defaults, and a header-cell cross-block range — never a cell rectangle. There is no range-runs test file, editor-range-style-summary.test.ts has no cell-rectangle case, and no test builds a cell rectangle indirectly via mouse events (only image-selection-overlay.test.ts uses mouse events in packages/docs/test). Searched exhaustively on the distinguishing token plus the keyboard-dispatch and mouse-drag entry points; found no counterexample.

finding.summary: Slides mobile toolbar's duplicated B/I/U toggle logic changed with no test
finding.evidence: `TextEditMobileBar` carries its own copy of the bold/italic/underline toggle + pressed-state logic (now reading `getRangeStyleSummary()` via `isStyleOn`). The diff adds dedicated regression tests for the other two copies of this logic (`tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` for the shared `TextFormatGroup`, `tests/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx` for the docs slim toolbar) but none for this one. Grepping packages/frontend/tests for `mobile-toolbar`/`TextEditMobileBar` returns no files, so nothing pins that this third copy inverts the range value rather than the caret value — it can silently regress to the caret-based bug.

verdict.reason: A dedicated regression test for the slides mobile toolbar's B/I/U logic does exist: packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/toolbar/mobile-text-toggles.test.ts, explicitly headed "Regression tests for issue #715 on the slides *mobile* toolbar" and noting that TextEditMobileBar "carries its own copy of the toggle logic - and therefore needs its own copy of the regression test." The reviewer's greps missed it because the file is named mobile-text-toggles (not mobile-toolbar) and imports the exported wrapper MobileSlidesToolbar rather than the internal TextEditMobileBar; a grep for isStyleOn across packages/frontend does in fact surface this test file, so the reviewer's second claimed search does not reproduce either. The test mounts the real component with state.kind === "text-edit", which mobile-toolbar.tsx:95 dispatches to TextEditMobileBar, so the real isStyleOn and Toggle logic executes and only the editor (a data boundary) is stubbed. The stub deliberately makes the caret style and the range summary disagree, then asserts for each of Bold/Italic/Underline that applyStyle receives the inverted *range* value (true when range unstyled but caret styled; false when range uniformly styled but caret unstyled; true when range mixed) and that aria-pressed follows the range and not the caret (false when caret styled but range unstyled, false for mixed, true for uniform). Under the caret-based bug the finding fears regressing to, those assertions fail - so the test genuinely pins the behavior and is neither vacuous nor over-mocked. It also runs in CI: vite.config.ts:268 includes tests/**/*.test.ts with jsdom environment at line 267.
